transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-09-29
- Start: 14:30 PDT
- Duration: 52 minutes (approx)
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Rina (Redwood CSM), Asha (Lighthouse Head of Data), Tom (Lighthouse ML Eng), Priyanka (PM), Ben (Security)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC sync focused on current quality heatmap, a spike of false positives in the billing intent classification task, and guardrail rule regressions after the last prompt change. Agreed to a short triage: Diego will export examples, Lighthouse will run a controlled staging run with recommended quantized profile, Redwood to propose a canary rollout and updated scoring spreadsheet.

Topics covered:
- Heatmap review and anomaly at prompt set "billing-clarify-v2"
- False-positive spike on 2025-09-26 after prompt templating change
- Scoring rubric drift: precision vs recall tradeoffs for high-severity intents
- Guardrail rule misfires (policy flags blocking benign responses)
- Performance implications of moving from hosted rwd-13b to dedicated q4 profile
- Next steps: exports, staging run, canary plan, pricing delta for burst capacity

Action items (captured verbally):
- Diego to pull top 200 false positives and label likely root cause; share CSV and short note. Due Thu 2025-10-01.
- Tom to run 1k-sample end-to-end on staging with rwd-13b-q4 quant profile; include latency traces and token-level costs. Due Fri 2025-10-03.
- Maya to circulate canary rollout plan and pricing delta for dedicated burst. Due Fri 2025-10-02.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Okay great, uh, thanks everyone for joining. We have about 50 minutes, wanna move quickly through the heatmap and then dig into the FP spike.
[00:18] Asha Menon: Yeah thanks, Maya. Quick context — we shipped the prompt template change on 9/25 and then on the 26th saw an uptick in through false positives in billing detection, like users asking about invoice breakdown being labeled as escalation.
[00:34] Diego Ramos: Mm-hmm, I pulled the quick charts. If you look at the confusion matrix, most of the mislabels moved from "info" to "escalate" after the templating tweak, so seems like a calibration shift.
[00:50] Tom Alvarez: Just to be clear, when you say templating tweak, that's the phrasing change where we add "if unsure, ask a clarifying question" right?
[01:02] Priyanka Rao: Yes, we added that line because product wanted the model to probe more. But maybe it's triggering the escalation intent.
[01:12] Maya Patel: Right that's the hypothesis. Diego, did you see anything in the logits or token probs that lines up?
[01:25] Diego Ramos: Uh, so the raw token probabilities are noisier post-change, there was more probability mass on tokens like "please escalate" or wording that the fine-tune associates with high severity. Could be a prefix bias — the model sees the clarifying prompt as leaning toward escalation. Also, we saw slight KV cache warm-up differences in the seq length distribution which might alter early token sampling.
[01:47] Asha Menon: KV cache warm-up, okay that's interesting — is that something we'd expect to fix with batching changes or is it model variant dependent?
[02:00] Diego Ramos: It can be both, but in our env the major lever is prompt engineering — shorten the prefix or make the probing conditional. Also the quant profile changes token rounding slightly, which in edge cases nudges argmax.
[02:15] Ben Kline: Quick security angle, we had one policy flag that flagged a perfectly normal support script as PII leakage after the template change — is that a false positive from the guardrail model or a ruleset misfire?
[02:29] Rina Cho: We saw that in the logs. Looks like the policy model bumped the score when the clarifying question included a user-provided identifier placeholder, the heuristic rule then jumped to block.
[02:40] Ben Kline: So it's a combination. We need to lower sensitivity or add exceptions for certain placeholders.
[02:48] Diego Ramos: We can add an exception in the guardrail rule for the pattern "<invoice_id>" or similar. But we should be careful — exceptions can create holes.
[02:58] Tom Alvarez: From the ML side, we tried reverting the prompt but that reduced recall on ambiguous billing queries, which product didn't like.
[03:10] Priyanka Rao: Right we can't regress on recall. Our success metric is > 92% precision on high-severity intents while keeping recall above 80% for billing detection.
[03:21] Maya Patel: Ok let's scope mitigations into three tracks: prompt surgical edits, guardrail rule tuning, and model/config adjustments (quant/profile). Diego, can you run the FP export?
[03:33] Diego Ramos: Yep, I'll include triple context: the original prompt, model output, and score deltas. I'll also flag whether the guardrail or classifier tripped first.
[03:43] Asha Menon: If possible, include user message examples anonymized — they help product understand the UX impact.
[03:50] Diego Ramos: Will do.
[03:53] Maya Patel: On the model/config side, Samir you had suggested trying the q4 quant profile on dedicated nodes to see if rounding shifts are the culprit?
[04:05] Samir Gupta: Yeah, the idea is to run a small staging batch with rwd-13b-q4 (we call it q4a in the doc) that reduces memory footprint and changes kernel selection; in past we've seen token-level differences but often not materially affecting high-level intent. But given this is borderline, it's worth testing.
[04:25] Tom Alvarez: What's the latency delta we'd expect? Our SLO is 250ms p95.
[04:31] Diego Ramos: On hosted with continuous batching we were at 210ms p95; dedicated q4 can be similar or slightly better but depends on our batch sizing. For the staging 1k sample we'll instrument traces.
[04:45] Priyanka Rao: Also pricing — if we need dedicated burst for the canary there's a delta we need to see.
[04:52] Maya Patel: I'll put numbers together and share the pricing delta for a 2-week burst.
[04:58] Asha Menon: Back to guardrails — the rule engine uses a lightweight classifier then heuristics. Can we decouple the block action from the classifier score and instead surface as a soft warn for three days?
[05:11] Rina Cho: Yes, Redwood Console supports a soft-fail mode and will produce audit logs but not block. That was actually recommended for early canaries.
[05:21] Ben Kline: Good, we prefer soft-fail until we've validated low noise. Need those audit logs forwarded to our SIEM — we use Splunk.
[05:29] Maya Patel: Diego, can you include the structured trace that shows event IDs for the guardrail hits so Lighthouse can ingest?
[05:36] Diego Ramos: Yeah I'll export logs in JSONL with event_id, rule_id, model_score, decision.
[05:43] Tom Alvarez: Small note — our anonymization pipeline strips email tokens; that might mask the placeholder behavior. We'll run with original messages in staging under NDA.
[05:54] Priyanka Rao: Okay, about the scoring rubric: we noticed that the numeric scoring weighted recall too low. Any way to make scoring more tunable per-intent?
[06:07] Maya Patel: The scoring spreadsheet has per-intent weight columns, but Diego can push a version with suggested weights that bias precision for billing-intent.
[06:16] Diego Ramos: I'll add a column with a recommended weight bump and run recalculation so you can see new precision/recall.
[06:23] Asha Menon: Would be helpful to see the threshold curves too, like PR curves for the last 30 days.
[06:29] Diego Ramos: I'll include PR curves and a small script to reproduce locally.
[06:34] Maya Patel: Quick question from R&D — when we talk about model variant names in the docs, sometimes the transcript will say rwd-13b-q4, sometimes open-13b — are there any confusions to clear for Lighthouse?
[06:46] Samir Gupta: We're testing our rwd-13b-q4 build (Redwood-built quant drop-in). It's not Open weights, it's our optimized kernels. Diego will detail the exact image.
[06:56] Tom Alvarez: On the user examples, we saw a cluster of false positives in UK region only — could this be a locale/language variant?
[07:07] Diego Ramos: Locale differences can influence tokenization slightly. I'll stratify the export by region.
[07:13] Priyanka Rao: Anything else on the heatmap?
[07:18] Asha Menon: There's one low-volume intent "refund_followup" that jumped, but it's lower priority than billing-escalate.
[07:25] Maya Patel: Ok. Let's outline the immediate rollback vs canary options. Diego?
[07:31] Diego Ramos: If you need a fast rollback, revert to the prior template and force a re-eval — that'll restore previous behavior but lose the probing benefit. Canary lets you keep the probe but funnel a small percent through a soft-fail guardrail and monitor.
[07:46] Priyanka Rao: We want the probing, so canary with soft-fail makes sense.
[07:51] Ben Kline: Security wants audit forwarding and an auto-sla to turn hard-block back on if any PII leakage observed.
[07:59] Rina Cho: We can configure an automated fallback policy that reverts to prior template if FP rate exceeds X for 4 consecutive hours.
[08:10] Maya Patel: Good. We'll propose thresholds in the canary doc.
[08:15] Asha Menon: On the false positives — any quick mitigation we can push now? Maybe a micro-prompt rule: don't tag escalation unless explicit escalation keywords present.
[08:28] Diego Ramos: Yep we can add a post-classification filter that requires either explicit escalation tokens or multiple signals. It's low-risk and quick.
[08:38] Tom Alvarez: That seems safe. Implement as a soft rule first.
[08:43] Maya Patel: Diego, add that to your export note as suggested mitigation.
[08:48] Diego Ramos: Will do.
[08:51] Priyanka Rao: A couple of engineering Qs: what telemetry will you need from us to evaluate the staging run?
[08:58] Diego Ramos: We'll need request/response pairs (anonymized), token-level timing, model variant, and guardrail event ids. A single zipped JSONL of 1k samples is ideal.
[09:10] Tom Alvarez: We can do that under the existing NDA and staging access.
[09:15] Maya Patel: Great. We're about 40 minutes in; let's run quick risk checklist.
[09:20] Ben Kline: Risk: PII leakage false negative if we loosen rules; we prefer soft-fail and short window. Also want retention of audit logs 90 days.
[09:31] Rina Cho: Redwood Console retention can be configured; I can share the doc.
[09:36] Priyanka Rao: Risk: UX regressions if recall drops — product will track NPS on support flows.
[09:42] Asha Menon: Risk: batch latency in dedicated may cause timeouts; ensure the canary uses realistic concurrency.
[09:51] Diego Ramos: We'll provide a recommended concurrency profile to mirror production.
[09:55] Maya Patel: OK last section — recap of decisions and next steps.
[10:00] Maya Patel: Decisions: run staging 1k with q4 profile; run soft-fail canary with post-classification filter; export top 200 FPs with root-cause labels; include PR curves and scoring spreadsheet update.
[10:14] Asha Menon: Agreed.
[10:17] Priyanka Rao: Agreed.
[10:19] Maya Patel: Any open questions before we close?
[10:22] Tom Alvarez: Only to confirm the canary percent — thinking 5% of traffic for 48 hours.
[10:29] Samir Gupta: 5% sounds reasonable; we recommend 1% to start scanning, then step to 5% after 6 hours if metrics stable.
[10:38] Ben Kline: Security approves as long as we have immediate revert and audit forwarding.
[10:45] Maya Patel: Great. We'll circulate notes and action items. Thanks everyone.
[10:51] Diego Ramos: Thanks all.
[10:55] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcript quality: automated transcription had trouble with some model/quant names (q4, q4a) and split some names, plus occasional word swaps (e.g., "escalate" vs "escape-late"), please rely on the action items and attachments for canonical references.
